title: Meet the CPU
about: What the processor does, what speed and cores really mean, and why it needs to stay cool.

cards.sentence: **GHz** is a CPU's speed: its clock ticks billions of times a second, doing tiny steps of work.

cards.prompt: The same CPU gets through more steps a second at 3 GHz than at 2 GHz.
cards.explanation: **True.** More GHz means more ticks each second, and every tick moves the work along, so the same CPU gets more done. (Real CPUs can even do several steps in one tick.)
cards.hint: The CPU does its steps as its clock ticks. Does 3 GHz mean more ticks or fewer?
cards.nudge: Look back at what GHz measures: does a bigger number mean more steps or fewer?

cards.sentence: A **core** is one worker inside the CPU, so a CPU with 4 cores can work on 4 things at once.

cards.prompt: Saving this video takes 12 seconds. Add cores to get it to **3 seconds or less**.
cards.explanation: A video is made of separate frames, so the work splits evenly between cores. One core takes 12 seconds, two take 6, and **four** take 3.
cards.hint: This job splits evenly, so each extra core takes a share. Watch the timer as you add cores.
cards.nudge: Keep adding cores and watch the timer. The job has to finish in 3 seconds or less.

cards.title: More cooks in the kitchen
cards.body:
Four cooks chop vegetables four times as fast. But four cooks can't bake a cake any sooner.

Cores are the same: they only help when a job **splits into pieces** that don't wait for each other.

cards.explanation: Photos and frames are separate pieces, so each core can take some. A treasure hunt and a scarf knitted row by row **need the step before**, so extra cores just wait.
cards.hint: For each job, ask: does every piece need the piece before it to be finished?
cards.nudge: Separate pieces can be shared out between cores. If each step needs the step before, extra cores just wait.

cards.prompt: Hard work makes the CPU hot. Tap the copper pipe.
cards.sentence: This **heat pipe** carries the CPU's heat away to metal fins by the vent.

cards.prompt: Tap the round part with blades.
cards.sentence: The **fan** blows air through those fins and out of the vents, so the CPU stays cool.
**Throttling** is when a CPU gets too hot and slows itself down to stay safe.

cards.prompt: Tap the **CPU** and the **two parts** that cool it.
cards.explanation: The **heat pipe** carries heat from the **CPU** to metal fins, and the **fan** blows air through them and out of the vents. If the vents are blocked, the heat stays in and the CPU throttles. Most phones have no fan: they spread the heat through their body, and throttle too.
cards.hint: You need three parts. The CPU is the small shiny chip. What carries heat away from it, and what moves the air?
cards.nudge: Tap all three: the CPU, the copper pipe that carries its heat, and the part that blows the air out.

cards.title: A real heat pipe

photo.alt: Inside a laptop: copper heat pipes curve from the processor area to a round fan.

cards.caption: Real **copper heat pipes** run from the processor (hidden under the plate) to the **fan**.

cards.prompt: On a soft blanket, the vents are blocked, so the CPU gets hot and ___.

options.nudge: Heat doesn't help a CPU. What does a too-hot CPU do to stay safe?
A CPU's cores are part of the chip, so it can't add any. What does a too-hot CPU do to stay safe?

cards.explanation: Blocked vents trap the heat, so the CPU **throttles**: it slows itself down to stay safe. A hard, flat surface lets the laptop breathe.
cards.nudge: Heat can't get out through blocked vents. What does a too-hot CPU do to stay safe?

cards.prompt: This laptop is throttling on a blanket, with a dusty fan. Get it back to **3 GHz**.
cards.explanation: The blanket blocked the vents, and dust clogged the fan and its fins. With both fixed, the heat can escape, so the CPU stops throttling and runs at full speed. (Laptop fans switch on by themselves; dust is what stops them cooling well.) Cleaning a fan means opening the laptop, so ask an adult or a repair shop to do it.
cards.hint: What's trapping the heat, and what's stopping the fan from moving air?
cards.nudge: A hot [[CPU]] slows itself down. Fix everything that traps heat or stops the fan cooling.

cards.prompt: A job can't be split. Which laptop finishes it first, if both run at 3 GHz?

options.nudge: Fewer cores don't make the one core doing this job any quicker. How many cores actually work on a job that can't be split?
Extra cores only help when a job can be split into pieces. This one can't, so how many cores actually work on it?

cards.explanation: A job that can't be split runs on **one core**, whichever laptop it's on. Each runs it on one core at 3 GHz, so they finish together. The 8-core laptop's extra cores only help with jobs that split.
cards.hint: Think of the cooks: can extra cooks help with a job that can't be split? Then compare the speeds.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- **GHz** is clock speed: more GHz, more steps a second.
- **Cores** only help with jobs that split into pieces.
- A hot CPU **throttles**. The heat pipe and fan keep it cool.

That's the [[hardware]]. Next: the software in charge.

**Try this:** use your laptop on a hard surface, not a bed, so its vents stay clear.
